extracted.intended_audience: Effective Altruism community members and prospective applicants interested in Survival and Flourishing Fund / Projects funding
extracted.subtask_description: A brief wiki-style overview of the Survival and Flourishing Fund (SFF) and Survival and Flourishing Projects (SFP) describing their mission, relationship, and typical grant recipients. Useful for people exploring funding opportunities or seeking basic eligibility/role information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mission: improve the long-term future
rubrics_metrics.description: Survival and Flourishing Fund (SFF) and Survival and Flourishing Projects (SFP) are two related entities that facilitate grants to projects aiming to improve the long-term future.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This states the overarching goal that grant-funded projects should address: improving the long-term future. No scoring guidance or examples are given on the page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organizational relationship and independence
rubrics_metrics.description: SFF and SAP share a common mission and leadership, and work closely with each other, but are not formally related and have different functions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates that although the entities coordinate, they operate separately and have distinct functions—applicants should be aware of which entity fits their proposal. The page provides no further procedural detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Typical recipient type — SFF
rubrics_metrics.description: SFF generally makes grants to existing charities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implies SFF primarily funds established charitable organisations rather than individuals or ad-hoc projects. The page gives no explicit eligibility criteria, amounts, or application process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Typical recipient type — SFP / SAP
rubrics_metrics.description: SFP makes smaller grants to individuals. (Page also uses the acronym 'SAP' in one place.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implies Survival and Flourishing Projects/SAP focuses on smaller, individual-directed grants. No details on grant size, scope, or selection criteria are provided on this page.
